dedupe_keys.name: centre for water systems benchmark water distribution networks

description: The Centre for Water Systems at the University of Exeter hosts a collection of benchmark problems used in the urban water modelling and optimisation literature, mostly water distribution networks that researchers have used to test design, rehabilitation and operation algorithms, some since the 1960s. Problems are grouped as expansion, layout, operation, and design and resilience; the page names networks such as Anytown, Hanoi, the New York tunnels, D-Town and Richmond, and real-world-derived cases such as the Wolf-Cordera Ranch development of Colorado Springs Utilities (1,981 pipes, 372 hydrants and 5 pumps). For each problem the collection gives a description and the simulation input file, for water distribution systems an EPANET file, plus other information needed to analyse it. The Centre maintains the page as a shared reference so that results in the literature can be reproduced and compared. Coverage is a set of synthetic or anonymised networks, not a geographic area, and the problems are static. Files are free downloads from the page; no licence is stated. Caveats: problem definitions and cost tables differ between papers that use the same network, and the networks are small compared with real utilities. Simulation uses: optimisation and capacity planning of network design, operational scheduling, network flow and resilience testing. Related records: LeakDB (data-leakdb), EPANET (model-epanet) and WaterModels.jl (model-watermodels-jl).
